contracts.blurb: Tailors down the road need Adire and Ankara bundles every week.
A Lagos store chain wants ready-cut Ankara for all its shelves.
Aso-ebi for 500 wedding guests, same Lace, same colour batch.
Upcountry wholesalers buying bales of George and Aso-oke.
Market women across the border reselling Naija Lace and Adire.
Diaspora brides and aunties paying pounds for a taste of home.

auto.name: Bale Forklift
auto.blurb: Offloads supplier bales from the truck with no porter sweating.

pack.name: Cut, Fold & Wrap Line
pack.blurb: Measures 6 yards, folds, labels and seals it for premium export.

milestones.title: Second Shop on the Island
milestones.blurb: Your first branch opens near the market. Customers no longer queue at one counter.

milestones.title: Lagos Aso-Ebi Circuit
milestones.blurb: Five stores from Island to Mainland. Party planners now call you first for aso-ebi.

milestones.title: The Name Tailors Trust
milestones.blurb: Ten branches. Tailors across Lagos send their customers straight to you.

milestones.title: Abeokuta Adire Connection
milestones.blurb: You buy direct from the dyers in Abeokuta, so Adire costs less and sells faster.

milestones.title: South-West Fabric Queen
milestones.blurb: Fifty stores from Ibadan to Akure. Every big owambe has your Lace on the dance floor.

milestones.title: Every State Wears Bola
milestones.blurb: A hundred branches from Kano to Port Harcourt. Your own trucks run the highways.

milestones.title: West Africa Opens Up
milestones.blurb: Stores in Accra, Cotonou and Lome. Traders cross borders to buy from your shelves.

milestones.title: Own Label Prints
milestones.blurb: Mills now print Ankara designs with your name on the selvedge. Nobody else has them.

milestones.title: Diaspora Flagships
milestones.blurb: Shops open in London and Houston. Brides abroad stop begging aunties to carry fabric.

milestones.title: Global Fabric Empire
milestones.blurb: 500 stores on three continents. From one market stall to a name the world wears.

staff: Who carry my tape rule again?
Aunty, this Lace na original o.
Abeg help me fold this George.
The Adire shelf don nearly finish.
Measure twice, cut once, my sister.
Fine colour! E go fit you well.
My scissors sharp pass my mouth.
Madam, this one just land today.
Next customer, I dey for you!
Careful, no stain the white Lace.
Small small, e go reach everybody.
customer: Madam, do customer price for me.
The Adire fine die, give me two.
My tailor said six yards, abi?
This Lace must match my gele o.
Show me your best George wrapper.
Aso-oke for my husband's cap too.
Last price? I be your customer.
My sister in London wants ten.
Same colour batch, no mix am o!
Chai, see quality! I'm coming back.
Add one extra yard as jara now.
manager: Oga, Lace stock is running low.
Count the yards, not the stories.
night: My feet tire, but my purse smile.
One day, a store in London too.
Small stall then, see me now.
Let me sleep, owambe season near.

events.name: Sharp New Scissors
events.text: Fresh scissors and tape rules for the team. Cutting is flying today!

research.claim: Idumota Market in Lagos is renowned for textiles including Ankara prints, lace, George and traditional wrappers, and is described as one of the oldest and largest markets in West Africa.
Balogun Market traders serve both retail and bulk buyers, and buyers of event (aso-ebi) quantities are advised to confirm yardage, width, dye fastness and colour batch before paying.
Handcrafted cotton adire from Abeokuta areas such as Itoku and Asero sells for roughly N4,000 to N15,000 and faces competition from cheap mass-printed imported imitations.
Ogun State launched an online adire portal so that buyers worldwide can place orders, reflecting export and diaspora demand for the cloth.
